thesis: Microsoft is the AI-capex bear market's poster child: operationally superb (Q3 FY2026 revenue $82.9B +18%, Azure +40%, AI run-rate $37B +123%) yet down ~30% from its $555 high after its worst month in 25 years, because ~$190B of calendar-2026 capex crushed quarterly FCF 22% to $15.8B and gross margin to its narrowest since 2022. The unusual disclosure that ~45% (~$281B) of its $625B backlog is tied to OpenAI adds a single-counterparty risk unprecedented at this scale. At 22.8x trailing - a discount to its recent history - the stock is the cheapest of the megacap AI spenders.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results (~late July 2026): guidance $86.7-87.8B revenue, Azure +39-40% cc
Sequential FCF-margin improvement - the explicit signal the capex cycle is peaking (CFO guided ~$190B CY2026 capex)
Microsoft 365 Copilot enterprise adoption metrics (the monetization bridge)
OpenAI relationship milestones or diversification of the $625B RPO base
risk_factors: OpenAI concentration: ~45% (~$281B) of remaining performance obligations tied to one customer whose own economics are unproven
Capex cycle: ~$190B CY2026 with Q4 above $40B; if it does not peak in 2026, FCF recovery slips and the multiple stays compressed
Gross margin 67.6% - narrowest since 2022 - as data-center depreciation mounts; Q4 operating margin guided down to 44%
Copilot enterprise adoption slower than expected (bear case flagged across coverage); hiring freeze in some cloud segments
